Pet insurance makes veterinary care more affordable

Costly veterinary care shouldn't get in the way of you getting the care your pet needs, but it often isn't in the budget. With pet insurance, we can help you manage unexpected vet bills when your cat or dog gets hurt or sick, while also covering the routine annual care they need to stay healthy.

What's covered?

Progressive offers a variety of pet insurance plans for dogs and cats, both directly and through our trusted provider, Pets Best. Learn more about each plan's coverages to determine which is right for your pet.

Plan availability varies by state.

Plan options

Extensive coverage plans

Accidents and illnesses

We offer plans that cover both injuries and illnesses, no matter how serious. These comprehensive plans cover:

Emergency care

Diagnostic testing

Specialist visits

And more

You can also customize your deductible, reimbursement percentage, and annual limit.

Wellness plans

Routine and preventive care

We offer wellness plans to help you pay for routine care without a deductible, including:

Wellness checkups

Vaccinations

Teeth cleaning

Accident Only plan

Accidental injuries

Pets Best offers an affordable, fixed-price pet insurance plan for broken bones, bite wounds, accidental swallowing of foreign objects, and other common unexpected injuries. This plan is designed for those on a budget who still want to make sure they can afford proper care for their dog or cat if they're injured.

Why choose Progressive for pet insurance?

SIMPLICITY

One deductible

You'll pay just one annual deductible per year, rather than one deductible per accident or illness claim, saving you more out of pocket.

Efficiency

Fast claims

Easily file claims online and receive your claim payment quickly for all eligible claims.

Affordable

Low-cost plans

You can easily build a pet insurance plan that fits your budget.

Common questions about pet insurance

Here are some frequently asked questions about pet insurance for cats and dogs:

Pet insurance is an insurance policy that can reimburse you for a portion of your pet's eligible vet bills. Learn more about how pet insurance works.

Unlike with health insurance for humans, there are no networks or copays for pet insurance. As long as your vet is a licensed veterinarian in the U.S., you can file claims for your eligible vet costs.

Pet insurance can be essential if you're unsure how you could afford expensive veterinary bills. Treatment for serious illnesses can be a financial burden without a pet insurance plan in place. Pet insurance wellness plans are a great option as well because they reimburse you for the routine care you're already spending on your pet each year, helping you keep them healthy while saving money.

In general, prices vary based on the age, breed, and location of your dog or cat. Your cost for pet insurance also depends on which types of coverage you want, as well as the reimbursement level and annual limit you select during enrollment. Learn more about the cost factors of pet insurance.

Choosing the right pet insurance for you depends on your budget and your pet's health needs. The most affordable plans only cover care for accidents, so many customers choose a more comprehensive plan option that covers treatment for both accidents and illnesses. There are also plan options that cover preventative care, which may be purchased separately or bundled with a more comprehensive plan, depending on the insurer. Learn more about shopping for pet insurance.

You can file a pet insurance claim once the waiting period for the applicable coverage is over, if there is one. A pet insurance waiting period is the amount of time after enrolling before your pet is eligible for coverage. Waiting periods vary by the type of coverage and start on the effective date of your policy. Once met, waiting periods are waived for continuous, uninterrupted policy renewals.

Progressive's waiting periods may vary but are typically:

Accidental injuries: No waiting period *

Illnesses: 15 days *

Orthopedic care: 30 days *

Wellness: No waiting period *

Pets Best's waiting periods may also vary but are typically:

Accidental injuries: 3 days *

Illnesses: 2 weeks *

Cruciate ligament conditions: 6 months *

Routine care (if added): No waiting period *

Pre-existing conditions aren't covered by most pet insurance companies. That's why pet insurance usually has waiting periods, to prevent customers from filing claims for issues that existed before the policy was active. Learn more about pre-existing conditions and pet insurance.

Pet insurance typically also doesn't cover dietary expenses and non-veterinary costs such as grooming and boarding.

Some insurers may allow you to add multiple pets to the same insurance policy, but most will require you to buy a separate policy for each pet. Each pet may also have a separate deductible and reimbursement level. Learn more about insurance for multiple pets.

Most pet insurers just cover cats and dogs. However, you may be able to find specialized pet insurance plans for exotic pets, such as birds or snakes.
